strings.name: Andrónico Luksic Craig
strings.role: Chilean businessman and former chairman of Quiñenco
strings.summary: Andrónico Luksic Craig is a Chilean businessman involved in his family group’s banking, industrial and international investments. He formerly chaired Quiñenco and was vice chairman of Banco de Chile. He progressively left major boards from 2023 and resigned as an Antofagasta director in 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026; the latest named report is dated November 5. Distinguishes his father Abaroa, Craig himself and his son Lederer; outdated roles are not retained as current, and family wealth is not personal net worth.
strings.influence.rationale: Participated in Chilean banking, industry and international investment, influencing corporate finance and industrial development in Latin America.
strings.facts.f1.label: Identity and education
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in Santiago, Chile, in 1954; attended Babson College. Sources differ on his degree, so no definitive qualification is stated here.
strings.facts.f2.label: Banking experience
strings.facts.f2.value: Vice chairman of Banco de Chile from 2002 to 2023; this was not the bank’s general-manager role.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Investment across sectors and borders
strings.highlights.h1.text: Helped expand financial and industrial businesses built on his father’s enterprise; achievements involved family members and professional teams.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Education and social support
strings.highlights.h2.text: Supported university exchanges, scholarships and child protection; philanthropic activities are recorded separately from corporate board roles.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Reported denial of impersonated investment promotions
strings.timeline.t1.text: BioBioChile reports his denial of fabricated online interviews and investment-platform endorsements; the false claims are not treated as biographical facts.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Leaves Antofagasta board
strings.timeline.t2.text: The company announces the following day that his resignation as non-executive director is effective; his son Lederer’s new appointment takes effect March 1.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Writes to resign as foundation vice chairman
strings.timeline.t3.text: Later reporting discloses a resignation letter dated this day and succession by his niece Isabella Luksic James; the letter date is not assumed to be the board’s effective date.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Leaves Quiñenco and other company boards
strings.timeline.t4.text: Resigns chairmanships including Quiñenco, CCU and LQIF, and leaves the boards of Banco de Chile, CSAV and Invexans.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Associated company buys remaining Canal 13 shares
strings.timeline.t5.text: Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile sells its remaining 33% stake to TV Medios, associated with him; the university announces the transaction November 6.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joins Antofagasta board
strings.timeline.t6.text: The UK register records the start of his directorship; a later company release confirms service as a non-executive director from 2013.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Becomes Quiñenco chairman
strings.timeline.t7.text: Succeeds after the death of his younger brother Guillermo, continuing international expansion of the group’s industrial and financial businesses.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Invests in Canal 13
strings.timeline.t8.text: TV Medios, associated with him, buys 67% of Canal 13 from Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile.
